column2: the super-parameter ordering face resolves the super constructor's parameter positions (an element-model question); the lexical face treats named super-parameters as in-order, so the out-of-order super-parameter shape stays silent
the inherited-member lookup is the same-file written-supertype chain — cross-file ancestors (imports, the SDK) never report (the dominant face); the primary-constructor parameter face stays unported
the non-literal arm's bool-ness reads the same-file written type — calls, chains, dynamic and nullable-written arms stay silent (the inference-bound family)

the static-type valid-use faces (Never-typed invocations, Future.error, Completer.completeError) stay silent (under-report); a shadowing local of the exception name inside a closure body counts as a use (over-report)
the inherited-instance-member skip walks the same-file ancestor chain — cross-file supertypes resolve to no instance members and the class reports
the binding face is the shadow-correct same-file walk — an import-bound identifier stays silent, and a prefixed or parameterized written type never resolves
a unicode escape (`\u{27}`) that produces a quote character in the official unescape is not seen on the raw segments (documented under-report)
an opaque receiver keeps the Iterable presumption (over-report); the null-aware chain bail reads the local chain only and misses exotic chains (under-report)
the nullable-declared-type gate is dropped — `int x = null;` (a compile error upstream) reports
the use count is unit-local — a typedef used only in sibling part files reports (the documented cross-file family)
the inherited concrete member is the same-file extends/with/on chain, concrete members only — cross-file inherited methods stay silent
the async `Future<void>` branch needs the resolved declared type, and the closure face with an inferred return type has no written type — both stay silent
the name set is the dart:core built-in list, so user-declared type names stay silent; primary-constructor declaring formals report (the official's no-hit shape)
the context type is the written-type chain — SDK callbacks and member targets resolve through the element model and stay silent (the dominant real faces)
the static-type face is the scalar-literal slice — identifiers, calls and collections are inference-bound and never report (the dominant face)
the official checks the library's file through the element model; dartq checks each unit, so a part file's own non-conforming name reports where the official judges the library

the ported face is the written-FunctionType assignment/initializer site — argument, return and collection sites, inferred targets and cross-file `call` classes stay silent (the dominant face); a bare-field user shadow over-reports

the interop classification is same-file `@JS` classes under a dart:js_interop import — other left expressions, cross-file interop types, the catch face and the js-side variants stay silent (the dominant face)
the `targetKinds` branch needs resolved `@Target` metadata, and a prefixed `foo.pragma` never matches the written core-pragma name — both stay silent
implicit field-formal/super-formal parameter types, extension `on`-clause and mixin constraint types, type-parameter bounds and prefixed (`p._Foo`) names stay silent (element-bound faces)

every string literal counts as valued and an unresolvable `is` name stays silent (under-report); a literal condition under a case clause reports — the clause is not read on the IfStatement row (over-report)
inferred-`bool` locals (`var x = true`) and `this.getter` receivers stay silent (the inference-bound family)
pattern-bound wildcard variables stay silent — their uses never enter the wildcard binding table
a member-chain receiver carries no written type and stays silent, and a bare same-file `print` skips the print face
the context face is the return / variable-initializer slice — argument and assignment contexts and the pattern face stay silent

an opaque receiver or type matches by written name outside the file — a user class reusing a core method name reports (the documented over-report residue); chained or computed receivers bail where the official resolves (under-report)
the inherited concrete member is the same-file chain — cross-file ancestors stay silent; the primary-constructor parameter face stays unported

pattern-assignment and cascade-section writes are not scanned, and the setter-override exemption is dropped (over-report); a same-named local mutation marks the field mutated, and cross-unit declaring formals stay silent (under-report)
a nested function literal shadowing the loop variable inside the invocation target keeps the lexical reference scan silent
a write bound to a shadowing redeclaration still counts (the erroneous family, under-report); `++`/`--` and pattern-assignment writes are not scanned (over-report)
the subtype check is written-type lexeme equality — differing-but-subtype spellings stay silent; a same-lexeme local over-counts and skips; private fields and primary constructors stay out
the parameter faces need the element model — argument and named-argument positions stay silent
an opaque operand keeps the String presumption — a user `operator+` class reports; multi-piece operands split piece-wise (report span only, gate-invisible)
an opaque receiver keeps the Iterable/Map/String presumption — a user `length` getter reports; `getIntValue` reads int literals only, so constant expressions stay silent

an opaque receiver keeps the core-family presumption — a user class with `isEmpty` but no `isNotEmpty` reports; a positional argument list carries no separators, so a later argument's access false-fires
the element pin is the written name — a prefixed `foo.deprecated` never matches; the `@Deprecated` class face is unreachable on valid code on both sides
if-case pattern variables are not walked — a read inside the then-branch of that name reports
the extraction reads a scheme prefix where `Uri.tryParse` rejects the malformed URI (broken IPv6 literals, invalid ports) — such a value reports where the official stays silent
the `hasInferredType` exemption reads initializer presence — a `dynamic`-typed initializer stays exempt where the official reports (the inference-bound face)
the element re-check is dropped — a nonexistent field or a mismatched written type (compile errors upstream) reports
the fenced-region toggle matches fence lines without tick-count matching — lines can flip in or out of the markdown code region either way
a constructor tear-off is no instance creation (both sides silent), and prefixed or chained receivers fail the bare-receiver check — the conservative family stays silent
the setter's write-type agreement guard is resolution-bound and dropped — a wrap whose written types disagree reports
the assignability gates are out of the same-file substrate — a type-mismatched tear-off reports (over-report); deferred-prefix targets stay silent at the bail (under-report)
the initializer face is the non-null literal slice — a non-null non-literal initializer stays silent until inference lands
the inherited member is the same-file chain (cross-file silent); the signature guard reads written shapes — subtype spellings and resolved defaults stay silent; the operator faces stay unported
the record-type exemption reads written types for variables only — parameter faces report; a TypeLiteral inner and the extension-nullable bail report (type-system faces dropped)
the getter and function-type faces resolve over the unit's own declarations — imported getters and core receivers stay silent (the conservative family)
the String-type question is answered only for a complete plain string literal — `$identifier` and multi-token expressions stay silent (the official corpus's main family)
the import bail keys on the written combinator shape — an import whose library does not actually export the name still silences the report
the Iterable-receiver gate is a lexical name check — a user `toList` on a non-Iterable (a compile error upstream in a spread) reports

the operand types are the scalar-literal/`this` slice — identifiers and calls stay silent; a user `==` override returning non-bool reports where the official's bool gate silences; the pattern face stays unported

the named-parameter conversion face needs the super constructor's resolved parameter list — named arguments never contribute, and a shadowing local over-counts body references (conservative, under-reports the conversion)

the target type reads `this.<field>` only — a bare field reports under shadowing (over-report); the right side is the scalar-literal slice and the return, pattern, argument and creation branches stay unported (under-report)
